title: Selection persistence across pages holds the elicited contract and announces the running count
asA: operator selecting rows across several pages before running a bulk action
iWant: the selection model to persist my row selections across pagination and announce the running count
soThat: cross-page bulk operations are visible and reversible

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given an operator elicited `selectionPersistence=cross-page` (ADR-1804), when the operator selects rows on page 1 and advances to page 2, the previously selected row ids remain in the selection model; a return to page 1 re-renders the checkboxes as checked. The check clicks a row checkbox, advances the page, returns, and asserts the checkbox is still checked. Applying agent sets: the project-specific bindings, routes, thresholds, budgets, and names named in the assertion.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a rendered datatable with elicited cross-page selection persistence
acceptanceCriteria.when: the operator selects rows on page 1 and paginates away and back
acceptanceCriteria.then: the row checkboxes on page 1 remain in the selected state on return

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a running row selection, the surface renders the current count in an accessible location adjacent to the bulk action controls; the count updates when a row is toggled without a full re-render of the surface.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a rendered datatable with at least one row selected
acceptanceCriteria.when: the operator toggles a second row
acceptanceCriteria.then: the accessible selection count updates by one without a full page re-render

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given the operator did not elicit cross-page persistence (ADR-1804's non-elicited default), the selection resets on pagination; the surface names this behaviour in the accessible copy near the bulk action control so operators are not surprised on advance. Applying agent sets: the project-specific bindings, routes, thresholds, budgets, and names named in the assertion.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a rendered datatable without cross-page persistence elicited
acceptanceCriteria.when: the operator selects rows and paginates away
acceptanceCriteria.then: the selection clears on advance and the accessible copy on the bulk-action region names the per-page-only behaviour

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given `selectionPersistence=cross-page` and the operator selects rows across pages then activates a bulk action, when the confirmation dialog opens the dialog's `aria-describedby` region names the total selected count (across pages) and the counts per page in a way the operator can verify before confirming; a dialog naming only the current page's count fails the pack check.
acceptanceCriteria.given: cross-page selection and an operator opening the bulk-action confirmation dialog
acceptanceCriteria.when: the pack inspects the dialog's aria-describedby content
acceptanceCriteria.then: the region names the total selected count across pages and per-page counts; a per-page-only count fails

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given `selectionPersistence=cross-page` and the operator selects rows on pages 1 and 2 then filters the visible rows down to a set that excludes some selected rows, when the pack inspects the selection model, the previously selected but now filtered-out row ids remain in the selection model (filter narrows presentation, not selection); the accessible chrome names the retained-but-hidden count so the operator can see the total.
acceptanceCriteria.given: cross-page selection followed by a filter that hides some selected rows
acceptanceCriteria.when: the pack inspects the selection model and accessible chrome
acceptanceCriteria.then: the hidden-but-selected row ids remain in the model and the chrome names the retained-but-hidden count

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given the selection model, when the operator invokes a `Clear selection` control, all selected row ids are removed, the running-count region announces zero, and every selection checkbox on the visible page returns to its unchecked state; the Clear selection control is keyboard-reachable and named `Clear selection` or an equivalent accessible name.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the operator activating the Clear selection control
acceptanceCriteria.when: the pack inspects the selection model and the visible checkboxes
acceptanceCriteria.then: all selected row ids are removed, the running-count region announces zero, visible checkboxes are unchecked, and the control is keyboard-reachable with an accessible name
